# Checklists

Read aloud, one line at a time, by the operator; the safety pilot answers. A line that cannot be answered stops the flight.

## Start of the day

- [ ] The day's coordinates are typed into the day file, read back by a second person against the organisers' sheet, and `verified: true`.
- [ ] `python3 tools/field_setup.py field/<day>.yaml --for-flight` wrote the day's files, and `summary.txt` has been held against the field map.
- [ ] The fence of the day is uploaded and read back (`sim/fence_upload.py --site field/<name>/site.yaml --url <link>`).
- [ ] `python3 tools/freeze_check.py --worktree` says `FREEZE HOLDS`.
- [ ] `platform/jetson/fallback.sh --check` says `CHECKLIST: 3 of 3 ok`: the 2026 fallback is ready.
- [ ] The ground laptop's clock is serving, and the companion follows it.
- [ ] Transmitter: the mode switch is where the safety pilot expects, the failsafe is set on the receiver.

## Before each flight: by hand

- [ ] The slot clock is running: `python3 tools/slot_clock.py start --slot <n>` on the ground laptop when the team is called (`show --watch` keeps its line on the screen), and the start time it prints is given to the aircraft.
- [ ] Props tight and undamaged; arms locked; nothing loose.
- [ ] Battery strapped, its plug seated; a fresh pack for every slot.
- [ ] The payload (or the hook) is the one for this mission, and is held.
- [ ] The camera's window and the rangefinder's are clean.
- [ ] The flight area is clear of people; the spotter has the aircraft in sight; the safety pilot has the transmitter in hand.

## Before each flight: the preflight

`tools/go.py` runs it and starts nothing on NO-GO. Each line below is one of its checks, with what GO means:

- [ ] **params**: The flight controller's parameters are the 2027 baseline's (`platform/fcu/argus_2027.param`), read from it or from a dump under 24 h old.
  - NO-GO: Load the baseline and upload the fence (`platform/fcu/README.md`), save a new dump, run the preflight again.
- [ ] **fence**: The fence is enabled and healthy, and its polygon is stored.
  - NO-GO: Upload the site's fence (`sim/fence_upload.py --site field/<name>/site.yaml`). Never fly without it.
- [ ] **gps**: A 3D fix or better, HDOP 1.4 or less, 8 satellites or more, in a reading under 2 s old (as every reading here must be).
  - NO-GO: Wait in the open, away from the tents and vehicles. An override here costs the missions that fly on GPS.
- [ ] **ekf**: The position estimate is healthy and the flight controller's own pre-arm checks pass.
  - NO-GO: Read the ground station's pre-arm message; it names what is wrong. Do not override.
- [ ] **rangefinder**: The downward rangefinder gives a reading and the flight controller says it has data.
  - NO-GO: Check its cable and its window. The drop and the delivery need it; a waypoint flight can be overridden.
- [ ] **cameras**: Each camera named is publishing at 80% of its mode's rate or more.
  - NO-GO: Check the ribbon cable and the camera service (`systemctl status argus-camera`), or the grabber the flight starts.
- [ ] **engine**: When the flight names an engine (`--engine`), the file is the one in the model registry (its sha256). With none named, nothing is compared and the line is GO.
  - NO-GO: Copy the registered engine again; an engine built on another machine is not used. A flight that uses a trained model must name its engine.
- [ ] **timesync**: The companion and the flight controller agree on the time (an estimate under 2 s old; nine in ten of its steps 20 ms or less and none over 100 ms), and the companion follows the ground laptop's clock when one is named (`--clock-source`).
  - NO-GO: Check the laptop's chrony and the network (`platform/jetson/clock_sync.py`). Stamped data on a clock that jumps is not flown on.
- [ ] **disk**: 20 GB or more free where the logs go.
  - NO-GO: Move old attempts off the disk (they are bundled: `attempts/`), not delete them on the field.
- [ ] **battery**: 3.9 V a cell or more, resting, on a 6-cell pack.
  - NO-GO: Change the pack. Never override: a pack that starts low does not finish a slot.
- [ ] **profile**: The flag profile fits the sequence: every flag declared, every dependency met.
  - NO-GO: Fix the profile or pick the sequence it was written for; `tools/go.py --dry-run` shows the same refusal.

An override (`--override "<reason>"`) is the lead's decision and is written with its reason and the operator's name in the preflight's log. The team's rule is that `fence`, `ekf` and `battery` are never overridden; the command does not enforce that, the people do.

## After each flight

- [ ] Disarmed, props stopped, before anybody walks out.
- [ ] The flight controller's log is pulled: `python3 tools/dataflash_pull.py --fc-url <link> --out <log folder>/<attempt>/dataflash`.
- [ ] The attempt is bundled: `python3 tools/bundle_attempt.py --slot <n> --mission <mission> --from-run <log folder>/<attempt>`, and it says `COMPLETE`.
- [ ] `python3 tools/post_flight.py attempts/<attempt>` is run; `NO HUMAN INPUT FOUND` is read out, or the findings are.
- [ ] The localisation's list is handed in within 30 minutes of the slot.
- [ ] The pack is on charge or set aside; a tuned value, if any, is committed with its `[tuning: <reason>]`.
